findings.source: CombatSystem.getEnemyAttackVisualState emits FormAttackPose: idle|windup|strike|recover. Enemy state internally idle|windup|cooldown; active is a player-weapon phase.
findings.consumer: costed-encounters allowObservedWindow line166 and caution lure-pass line186 compare enemy attack to active. That branch can never match.
findings.runtime: Two original severe observer logs contain17 strike observations and0 active. All8 accepted observed-back-facing-window events contain only idle, so no accepted-strike window is proven in this pair.
findings.minimumCorrection: In a newly versioned supplementary controller, compare the actual strike enum instead of active at both predicates; add a focused real-contract negative case. Keep original policy15 and its SHA unchanged.
findings.causalLimit: The correction is conservative and has no demonstrated path to solve the two failed searches. It cannot justify replaying unchanged originals or claiming a player bug.

findings.source: catalog image_lure creates a visible body at cast position for its paid duration; it never adds enemy movement suppression. AI visibleDecoyFor and sightTargetPos explicitly decline to override confirmed CHASE toward the real player. Sound lure also does not erase CHASE.
findings.consumer: evade() spends an image_lure under break-visible-pursuit and moves54px candidates; its paid-use boolean is ignored. Only sound_lure receives lurePass; image_lure does not. Generic visible back-facing observations can still grant short movement windows.
findings.runtime: The two original branches spent2/4 mirrors; mere uses spent does not prove any enemy saw or targeted a decoy. The logs deliberately do not read hidden AI targets. Both search calls rejected currently close visible enemies.
findings.minimumCorrection: Do not treat paid mirror activation as a safe search window, freeze, or successful aggro reset. If root authorizes a new generic policy, record own paid effect position/lifetime and require actual rendered enemy motion/facing away before approaching; retain strike/windup rejection. This is a separate changed policy, not a guard-only correction.
findings.causalLimit: Cannot prove the mirror produced a usable search window in these originals without observed movement context; no automatic safe-enemy filtering is warranted.

findings.source: solidify can stop perception/movement/attack and breaks on damage; weak wax_sealed_button lasts1000ms, normal versions2500/4000/5500ms. Tripwire only sets movementMultiplier0 on an actual crossing; it does not suppressAttack.
findings.consumer: search/caution assume2500ms stoppedUntil for a selected enemy after any matching paid solidify use, without binding actual target, duration or damage break. Tripwire is only used via evade; it is not added to stoppedUntil.
findings.runtime: Neither solidify nor tripwire is equipped in these two original processes; this cannot explain their loss/empty return.
findings.minimumCorrection: A future independent controller should bind its own paid solidify receipt and actual visible target/duration/break before granting an attack-safe channel. Never promote tripwire movement stop to attack suppression.
findings.causalLimit: Not part of the current white-scarfield fix; do not expand scope without separate root decision.

recommendation: Retain the two failed original outcomes and all policy15 inputs. No product/CSV change is supported by this audit. The enum bug is a real but noncausal narrow controller contract issue. Any exploration/paid-effect strategy improvement requires a separately frozen supplementary protocol and actual same-world/seed evidence; it cannot be labelled original policy15.
